data.content_ref: inline:The target frames the nocturnal UHI as arising primarily from reduction of evapotranspiration/latent heat loss, but on a clear, calm night the dominant differential mechanism is urban thermal storage and reduced sky-view factor: cities release stored sensible heat from high thermal-capacity materials and trap longwave radiation in street canyons, whereas countryside cools efficiently by direct longwave radiative loss to the sky. Latent heat flux is typically weak at night in both environments (stomata largely closed, low available energy), so evapotranspiration reduction is a daytime differential, not the principal nocturnal one. The cross-city modulation is likewise attributed to green space/irrigation/humidity, yet the largest, most robust cross-city modulator of the nocturnal UHI is urban geometry (sky view factor / street canyon depth), which the target omits as a causal driver despite being a named commitment surface. This misattributes the core mechanism the problem asks for.
